title: Obesity, morbid obesity and BMI
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's weight diagnosis and BMI, if reportable.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for weight management.

HPI
Pt is an 87 y/o female presenting for scheduled follow-up regarding obesity. Pt reports difficulty with weight loss despite some attempts at lifestyle modification. She notes mild fatigue but denies any acute symptoms or shortness of breath. She is motivated to improve her current health status.

Medication List
Multivitamin daily
Vitamin D3 1000 IU daily

Exam
Vitals: BP 132/78, HR 74, RR 16, Temp 98.6F, BMI 52.8.
Gen: Well-appearing, alert, and oriented x3.
CV: RRR, CTAB.
Lungs: Clear to auscultation.
Ext: No edema noted.

Assessment
1. Obesity. Pt remains at a high BMI of 52.8.

Plan
Discussed weight management goals. Provided extensive counseling on dietary modifications, focusing on caloric deficit and balanced nutrition. Encouraged increased physical activity as tolerated by her physical capabilities. Pt to f/u in 3 months for weight check.

Electronically signed, R. Mensah, DO, 05/14/2026
explanations: Obesity documented by the provider: E66.9. The coder does not upgrade it to morbid obesity from the BMI.
BMI 52.x with a provider weight diagnosis: add Z68.43 (BMI 40 or more maps to HCC 48 on its own).

distractors.why: Only the provider can diagnose morbid obesity; the BMI does not change the diagnosis.
The BMI is documented and the provider diagnosed the weight condition: add the Z68 code.
